beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:storytelling, a twinkle]In the {1930s|nineteen thirties}, in Costa Rica, bulldozers clearing jungle for ^banana plantations hit something ^round. [act:the reveal, simply][tune:fall]^Stone balls. [act:widening, wonder][tune:fall]^Hundreds of them.
[d:tension][act:marvelling, slow][tune:level]Some ^taller than a person. [act:hushed wonder][tune:fall]Almost ^perfectly round. [act:curious, the hook][tune:rise]Who made them, and ^why?

[d:calm][act:orienting, calm]This is the Diquís ^Delta, near Costa Rica's ^Pacific coast, where a river fans out into many channels before it meets the ^sea. [act:giving the range, clear]More than three hundred spheres are known here, from a few ^centimetres to two and a half ^metres across, from the size of a tennis ball to taller than a ^door.

[d:build][act:matter of fact, confident]They were made over about nine ^centuries, from about AD {600|six hundred}, by local ^chiefdoms: communities led by chiefs. [act:admiring the craft]Hard rock, ^pecked and ground into shape with ^harder stones. [act:a picture, wry]Think of sanding wood, only ^far slower.

[d:build][act:intrigued, setting up the claim]Some spheres stand in ^lines. [act:reporting the claim, fairly]Lines that point at ^solstice sunrises, say some writers. [act:explaining, simple]A solstice is the longest, or the shortest, day of the ^year. [sfx:shimmer][act:the bolder claim, even]Or ^sea routes, encoded by a lost ^ocean-going culture, says one book from {1998|nineteen ninety-eight}. [p:0.93][act:fair, the strongest case]And it's tempting: people who took such care over the ^shape of a stone may well have cared where it ^stood.

[d:build][act:the snag, plainly]But almost every sphere was ^moved before anyone ^mapped it. [act:where they went, a little rueful][tune:fall]Rolled away to ^plantations, ^gardens and ^government buildings. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Reading their lines now is like reading a sentence after someone has ^shuffled the words.
[d:aside][act:a wry aside, quicker]Treasure hunters even ^dynamited a few, hoping for ^gold inside. [act:deadpan, understated][tune:fall]There was ^none.

[d:reveal][sfx:hit][act:the insight, leaning in]And here's the catch: with two or three points, ^any line points at ^something. [act:counting them off, lightly][tune:level]A ^sunrise. [act:same rhythm][tune:level]A ^moonrise. [act:the punchline, dry][tune:fall]A ^mountain.

[d:build][act:precise, careful]The real test asks: would random lines do just as ^well? [act:precise, careful]No ^published survey@noun has tested the lines still in place against ^chance. [go:5|0][act:fair, even-handed][tune:fall]^Untested isn't the same as ^false.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]Lines aimed at the ^sky? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]*Awaiting ^evidence*. [act:the grounded option][tune:rise]Symbols of ^power, in chiefs' villages? [act:plain and assured][tune:fall]That's what the ^digs show.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:warm, an open invitation]The test is ^simple, and the lines at Finca Six are still ^waiting.
